title: A surface that folds
hook: Two surfaces can fit in the same space.

doesNotKnow: In this schematic, which surface has more exposed edge available for exchange: a smooth edge or a folded edge?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: In this schematic, which surface has more exposed edge available for exchange: a smooth edge or a folded edge?

claims.text: In this schematic, which surface has more exposed edge available for exchange: a smooth edge or a folded edge? The folded edge exposes more boundary within the same width in this drawing. Gill filaments and their smaller lamellae increase the surface available for gas exchange. The drawing is a geometry schematic, not a measurement of a fish gill.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, animal respiration and osmoregulation, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A thin sheet is folded repeatedly without hiding its surfaces. What can increase inside the same footprint? Folding can increase exposed surface area within a limited footprint.
